neighbours.label: verbs of stopping or ceasing an ongoing activity (stop, stopped, ceased)
fire: After the second warning, the children finally stopped shouting in the hall.
Doctors told him he should stop drinking coffee late at night.
The old factory ceased production in the spring of 1987.
Once the rain stops falling, we can walk down to the harbour.
At some point you have to stop worrying about things you can't change.
The clock in the tower stopped ticking years ago.
Many readers stopped buying the paper when the price went up.
The company will stop shipping orders to that region next month.
quiet: After the second warning, the children kept shouting in the hall.
Doctors told him he should drink less coffee late at night.
The old factory expanded production in the spring of 1987.
Once the rain is falling, we can listen to it from the harbour.
At some point you have to accept things you can't change.
The clock in the tower has been ticking for years.
Many readers kept buying the paper when the price went up.
The company will begin shipping orders to that region next month.

notes: Card: ' stop' and ' stopped' are the peak token of 20 of the top 32, plus ' ceased' and '停止'. The + pole is the other side: 'start'/'starting'. Near misses describe continuing activities.
